questions.knowledgeNote: Regroup into the three projection pairs: (b*cosA + a*cosB) = c and friends.
questions.question: Q3(a). In any triangle, prove that (b+c)*cosA + (c+a)*cosB + (a+b)*cosC = a + b + c.
questions.solution: Regroup the left side as (b*cosA + a*cosB) + (c*cosB + b*cosC) + (a*cosC + c*cosA). By the projection law b*cosA + a*cosB = c, c*cosB + b*cosC = a, and a*cosC + c*cosA = b. Adding gives c + a + b = a + b + c.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q3(a); book p186 = PDF p213-214 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Write everything with a = 2R*sinA: both sides become 8R^2*sinA*sinB*sinC.
questions.question: Q3(b). In any triangle, prove that b^2*sin2C + c^2*sin2B = 2ab*sinC. (T.U. 2051H)
questions.solution: Left side: b^2*2*sinC*cosC + c^2*2*sinB*cosB = 8R^2*sin^2B*sinC*cosC + 8R^2*sin^2C*sinB*cosB = 8R^2*sinB*sinC*(sinB*cosC + cosB*sinC) = 8R^2*sinB*sinC*sin(B+C) = 8R^2*sinA*sinB*sinC. Right side: 2*(2R*sinA)*(2R*sinB)*sinC = 8R^2*sinA*sinB*sinC. Both sides agree.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q3(b) (T.U. 2051H); book p186 = PDF p214 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: The trick is (b*cosC + c*cosB)^2 = a^2: expand it to isolate c^2*cos^2B + b^2*cos^2C.
questions.question: Q3(c). In any triangle, prove that c^2*cos^2B + b^2*cos^2C + bc*cos(B-C) = (a^2 + b^2 + c^2)/2. (T.U. 2058S)
questions.solution: From the projection law a = b*cosC + c*cosB, squaring gives a^2 = b^2*cos^2C + c^2*cos^2B + 2bc*cosB*cosC, so c^2*cos^2B + b^2*cos^2C = a^2 - 2bc*cosB*cosC. Substituting: left side = a^2 - 2bc*cosB*cosC + bc*cos(B-C) = a^2 - 2bc*cosB*cosC + bc*(cosB*cosC + sinB*sinC) = a^2 - bc*(cosB*cosC - sinB*sinC) = a^2 - bc*cos(B+C) = a^2 + bc*cosA. Since bc*cosA = (b^2+c^2-a^2)/2, this is a^2 + (b^2+c^2-a^2)/2 = (a^2+b^2+c^2)/2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q3(c) (T.U. 2058S); book p186 = PDF p214 (vision read; the 1/2 on the right confirmed in print)

questions.knowledgeNote: c - b*cosA = 2R*sinA*cosB: the sinA factor cancels in the ratio.
questions.question: Q3(d). In any triangle, prove that (c - b*cosA)/(b - c*cosA) = cosB/cosC. (HSEB 2064)
questions.solution: c - b*cosA = 2R*sinC - 2R*sinB*cosA = 2R*[sin(A+B) - sinB*cosA] = 2R*sinA*cosB. Likewise b - c*cosA = 2R*sinB - 2R*sinC*cosA = 2R*[sin(A+C) - sinC*cosA] = 2R*sinA*cosC. Dividing (cosA != 0; if cosA = 0 both numerator and denominator reduce via the projection law) gives cosB/cosC.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q3(d) (HSEB 2064); book pp186-187 = PDF pp213-214 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Same 2R expansion as Q3(d): a - b*cosC = 2R*sinC*cosB, and the cosB cancels.
questions.question: Q3(e). In any triangle, prove that (a - b*cosC)/(c - b*cosA) = sinC/sinA.
questions.solution: a - b*cosC = 2R*sinA - 2R*sinB*cosC = 2R*[sin(B+C) - sinB*cosC] = 2R*cosB*sinC. From Q3(d), c - b*cosA = 2R*sinA*cosB. Dividing gives (2R*sinC*cosB)/(2R*sinA*cosB) = sinC/sinA.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q3(e); book p187 = PDF p214 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Use cosB = (a^2+c^2-b^2)/(2ac): each product a^3*b*cosC collapses to a^2*(a^2+b^2-c^2)/2.
questions.question: Q4(a). In any triangle, prove that a^3*sin(B-C) + b^3*sin(C-A) + c^3*sin(A-B) = 0.
questions.solution: Write sin(B-C) = sinB*cosC - cosB*sinC = (b*cosC - c*cosB)/(2R), so a^3*sin(B-C) = a^3*(b*cosC - c*cosB)/(2R). Summing cyclically and multiplying by 2R gives [a^3*b*cosC + b^3*c*cosA + c^3*a*cosB] - [a^3*c*cosB + b^3*a*cosC + c^3*b*cosA]. Now a^3*b*cosC = a^3*b*(a^2+b^2-c^2)/(2ab) = a^2*(a^2+b^2-c^2)/2, and cyclically; their sum is (1/2)*[sum a^4 + sum a^2*b^2 - sum a^2*c^2] = (1/2)*sum a^4 since the two mixed sums are equal. Likewise a^3*c*cosB = a^2*(a^2+c^2-b^2)/2, summing to the same (1/2)*sum a^4. Their difference is 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q4(a); book p187 = PDF p214 (vision read; cubes confirmed: a^3, b^3, c^3)

questions.knowledgeNote: [(b^2-c^2)/a^2]*sin2A reduces to 2*sin(B-C)*cosA; then sin(B-C)*cosA = (sin2C - sin2B)/2 telescopes.
questions.question: Q4(b). In any triangle, prove that [(b^2-c^2)/a^2]*sin2A + [(c^2-a^2)/b^2]*sin2B + [(a^2-b^2)/c^2]*sin2C = 0.
questions.solution: (b^2-c^2)/a^2 = 4R^2*sin(B-C)*sinA/(4R^2*sin^2A) = sin(B-C)/sinA, so the first term is [sin(B-C)/sinA]*2*sinA*cosA = 2*sin(B-C)*cosA (and cyclically). Now 2*sin(B-C)*cosA = 2*[sin(B-C+A) + sin(B-C-A)]/2 = sin(pi-2C) + sin(-(pi-2B)) = sin2C - sin2B. Summing cyclically: (sin2C - sin2B) + (sin2A - sin2C) + (sin2B - sin2A) = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q4(b); book p187 = PDF p214 (vision read; denominators a^2, b^2, c^2 confirmed)

questions.question: Q4(c). In any triangle, prove that (a^2-b^2+c^2)*tanB = (a^2+b^2-c^2)*tanC = (b^2+c^2-a^2)*tanA.
questions.solution: a^2 - b^2 + c^2 = 2ac*cosB by the cosine rule, so the first expression is 2ac*cosB*tanB = 2ac*sinB = 2ac*(b/2R) = abc/R. Cyclically the second is 2ab*sinC = abc/R and the third is 2bc*sinA = abc/R. All three equal abc/R, hence are equal.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q4(c); book p187 = PDF pp214-215 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Sum-to-product on top and bottom: cosB - cosC = -2*cos(A/2)*sin((B-C)/2), cosA + 1 = 2*cos^2(A/2).
questions.question: Q4(d). In any triangle, prove that (cosB - cosC)/(cosA + 1) = (c - b)/a.
questions.solution: cosB - cosC = -2*sin((B+C)/2)*sin((B-C)/2) = -2*cos(A/2)*sin((B-C)/2), and cosA + 1 = 2*cos^2(A/2). So the left side is -sin((B-C)/2)/cos(A/2). Meanwhile (c-b)/a = (sinC - sinB)/sinA = [2*cos((B+C)/2)*sin((C-B)/2)]/[2*sin(A/2)*cos(A/2)] = [2*sin(A/2)*(-sin((B-C)/2))]/[2*sin(A/2)*cos(A/2)] = -sin((B-C)/2)/cos(A/2). Both sides agree.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q4(d); book p187 = PDF p215 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Numerator = 2R*sum sin^2, denominator = abc/(2R^2): their ratio is exactly R*(a^2+b^2+c^2)/(abc).
questions.question: Q4(e). In any triangle, prove that (a*sinA + b*sinB + c*sinC)/(a*cosA + b*cosB + c*cosC) = R*(a^2+b^2+c^2)/(abc).
questions.solution: Numerator: a*sinA + b*sinB + c*sinC = 2R*(sin^2A + sin^2B + sin^2C) = 2R*(a^2+b^2+c^2)/(4R^2) = (a^2+b^2+c^2)/(2R). Denominator: a*cosA + b*cosB + c*cosC = 2R*(sinA*cosA + sinB*cosB + sinC*cosC) = R*(sin2A + sin2B + sin2C) = R*4*sinA*sinB*sinC = 4R*(a/2R)*(b/2R)*(c/2R) = abc/(2R^2). Dividing: [(a^2+b^2+c^2)/(2R)]/[abc/(2R^2)] = R*(a^2+b^2+c^2)/(abc).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q4(e); book p187 = PDF p215 (vision read)
